wf.text: The waterfall model runs the phases in order. Each phase is done once, and the next starts only when the previous one is complete.

wfgood.text: It is simple, easy to manage, and it works well for small projects whose requirements are well understood.

wfbad.text: But every requirement must be known up front. And major problems are found late, in testing.

idle.text: There is no parallelism, so people sit idle, waiting for others.

iter.text: The fix is iterative development. Build a part, test it, get feedback, then build more. Each iteration does some analysis, some design, some coding, and some testing.

par.text: Iterations can even run in parallel, with separate teams.

agile.text: Agile is a highly iterative process. Its purpose: speed up development, and respond to change.

v1.text: Agile values individuals and interactions over processes and tools. And working software over comprehensive documentation.

v2.text: Customer collaboration over contract negotiation. And responding to change over following a plan.

agpro.text: Every iteration produces working software. So the customer can see the project, and give better requirements.

agcon.text: The risks: agile is problematic for very small and very large projects, and documentation takes second place.
